documents.title: APU AI Policy: Responsible and Ethical AI Use
documents.summary: Student-facing university AI policy for APU with purpose, definitions, permitted and prohibited uses, citation rules, faculty discretion, consequences and a long FAQ. AI is allowed for brainstorming, study aids and editing only with explicit instructor permission and disclosure.
documents.stance_why: Permitted uses are allowed 'only with explicit instructor permission and proper disclosure/citation' and violations include 'submitting AI-generated content as original without permission', so AI is barred unless permitted for narrow listed uses (restrict). Course rules are left to instructors ('Instructors set course-specific AI policies') but the document itself sets this baseline.

units.why: The opening says the policy 'promotes responsible AI use ... as a learning aid' and 'requires transparent disclosure'; it is a university-wide statement of purpose and principles, so P56 and general/informs.
units.anchor: promotes responsible AI use (like Google Gemini and NotebookLM) as a learning aid

units.why: The definition of AI tools sets what the policy covers ('Software, applications, or platforms that can perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence'), so it is a P61 definition.
units.anchor: Software, applications, or platforms that can perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence

units.why: Defines generative AI as tools 'capable of creating new content (e.g., text, images, code, audio)', which sets the policy's scope; P61 definition.
units.anchor: AI tools capable of creating new content (e.g., text, images, code, audio)

units.why: Defines knowledge-management/research AI such as NotebookLM, extending the scope to tools that analyze user-provided sources; P61 definition.
units.anchor: AI tools designed to analyze, organize, summarize, and extract information from existing

units.why: Permitted uses are allowed 'only with explicit instructor permission', so the default is that AI is barred unless the instructor allows it. Chosen as P06 (fallback when permission is absent) because the sentence does not itself hand a choice to each instructor (that is the Faculty Discretion unit, P04).
units.anchor: only with explicit instructor permission and proper disclosure/citation
units.policy: Students may use AI only with explicit instructor permission and proper disclosure/citation.

units.why: Lists the uses that can be permitted: 'brainstorming, research support, grammar/style editing, study aids, and learning/exploration'. It names learning-oriented uses (tutor-like exploration and study aids) rather than code, so P12 is the closest fit; the permission condition is coded in the unit above.
units.anchor: Students may use AI for brainstorming, research support, grammar/style editing, study

units.why: 'Violations include submitting AI-generated content as original without permission' bars passing off AI output as one's own work, which is P19; P36 does not fit as well because the point is what students may not submit.
units.anchor: submitting AI-generated content as original without permission

units.why: The list of violations includes 'violating data privacy', a prohibition on privacy-violating AI use. P50 (protect personal data) fits; no more specific rule is given.
units.anchor: circumventing learning objectives, and violating data privacy
units.policy: AI use that violates data privacy is a violation of the policy.

units.why: The prohibited list includes 'circumventing learning objectives': a ban on using AI to bypass the learning the work is meant to produce. P32 (students stay the primary problem-solver) is closest; P41 would require an explicit statement that AI shortcuts practice.
units.anchor: circumventing learning objectives
units.policy: Circumventing learning objectives with AI is a violation of the policy.

units.why: 'When permitted, students must clearly disclose and properly cite AI tool use' is a mandatory disclosure and citation rule, P24.
units.anchor: clearly disclose and properly cite AI tool use (e.g., on title page and in-text)

units.why: Students 'must also be prepared to provide prompts and raw AI output if requested', which asks for the prompt and the output on demand; P25 fits (specific details) better than P26 (full logs kept and submitted).
units.anchor: They must also be prepared to provide prompts and raw AI output if requested.

units.why: The example in-text citation includes the model, year and prompt, showing what the citation must contain; coded P25 as informational.
units.anchor: (Google Gemini, 2025; prompt: “Explain the causes of the American Civil War”)

units.why: 'Instructors set course-specific AI policies' hands the decision to instructors, P04.
units.anchor: Instructors set course-specific AI policies

units.why: 'students must follow these and seek clarification when questions arise' binds students to the course policy and tells them to ask; P10 is the best fit.
units.anchor: students must follow these and seek clarification when questions arise
units.policy: Students must follow the course-specific AI policies and seek clarification when questions arise.

units.why: 'Students are responsible for the originality, accuracy, and integrity of all submitted work' makes students own what they submit, P29.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for the originality, accuracy, and integrity of all submitted

units.why: 'Always verify AI-generated information, critically evaluate output' requires checking AI output, P31.
units.anchor: Always verify AI-generated information, critically evaluate output

units.why: 'ensure the final work reflects your own critical thinking' keeps the student as the thinker, P32.
units.anchor: ensure the final work reflects your own critical thinking

units.why: 'Policy violations are academic integrity breaches, leading to disciplinary action' classifies misuse as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Policy violations are academic integrity breaches, leading to disciplinary action

units.why: The closing says students 'are expected to use AI tools as faithful stewards, maintaining integrity'; a framing principle for the whole policy, tied to the Christ-centered mission, so P56.
units.anchor: Students are expected to use AI tools as faithful stewards, maintaining integrity

units.why: FAQ: 'When in doubt, always ask your professor' tells unsure students to ask first, P10.
units.anchor: When in doubt, always ask your professor.
units.frag_end: understand and follow those specific guidelines.

units.why: 'Every course and every instructor may have different expectations' states that policy varies by course and one course's rule does not carry over, P11.
units.anchor: Every course and every instructor may have different expectations for AI usage.

units.why: The FAQ says 'any use of AI to generate content ... is not considered original work and must be properly cited and attributed': a disclosure and citation rule, P24.
units.anchor: must be properly cited and attributed

units.why: 'APU supports the transparent and ethical use of generative AI tools' states the university's overall welcoming-with-conditions position, a framework statement P56 (not P02, because it is not an unconditional default).
units.anchor: APU supports the transparent and ethical use of generative AI tools.
units.frag_end: ethical use of generative AI tools.

units.policy: Using AI tools such as Gemini to generate a complete paper or assignment is a violation of APU’s academic integrity policy.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (A.I.) Classroom Use Policies: A Syllabus Resource for Instructors
documents.summary: A syllabus resource from the Office of Curricular Support offering instructors three ready-made AI syllabus statements (no, partial, full AI use) and a three-level scale plus a list of strategies for redesigning assignments. It predates the fall 2025 policy.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no single rule; it gives instructors three options ('Instructors can choose one of three use options to include in their syllabus'), so it delegates the decision to each course and lists the tiers.

units.why: The intro says the revised integrity policies 'stipulate that any use of A.I. tools must have prior instructor permission': AI is off unless permitted. P06 (rule when a syllabus is silent) fits better than P01 since permission can be granted.
units.anchor: any use of A.I. tools must have prior instructor permission
units.policy: Any use of A.I. tools must have prior instructor permission.

units.why: 'Instructors can choose one of three use options to include in their syllabus' defines three named tiers (No / Partial / Full), P05.
units.anchor: Instructors can choose one of three use options to include in their syllabus.

units.why: The statements 'are also being added to Syllabus Templates' on the OCS website, so ready-made syllabus AI language is provided; P09 is closest (AI statement in syllabus), though it is not a requirement.
units.anchor: These statements are also being added to Syllabus Templates

units.why: Option 1 states 'the use of any artificial intelligence (A.I.)-powered programs, unless specifically assigned, is not allowed': a ban for the course, P01.
units.anchor: unless specifically assigned, is not allowed

units.why: 'Any use of A.I.-generated work to outline, write, create, or edit ... is an academic integrity violation' classifies misuse as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: is an academic integrity violation

units.why: Option 1 lists 'A.I. writing assistant tools like Grammarly, Quillbot, and WordTune' as covered tools, a rule on prose tools; P18.
units.anchor: A.I. writing assistant tools like Grammarly, Quillbot, and WordTune

units.why: Option 1 gives the reason that A.I. programs 'may provide inaccurate or biased information, and they do not serve your academic development', a learning rationale; P41.
units.anchor: they do not serve your academic development

units.why: 'please ask your instructor' if not sure a resource violates the policy, P10.
units.anchor: if a resource you have found will violate this policy, please ask your instructor

units.why: Option 2 states that students 'can use A.I.-powered programs ... to support, not replace, your efforts', keeping the student as primary worker, P32.
units.anchor: to support, not replace, your efforts in completing your assignments
units.frag_start: In this course, you can use

units.why: Option 2 frames 'Learning to use artificial intelligence (A.I.)-powered programs is an emerging skill', a skill rationale, P44.
units.anchor: is an emerging skill

units.why: 'Your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited' is a disclosure rule, P24.
units.anchor: Your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited

units.why: 'AI is not likely to generate a response that would be seen as quality work and should be modified and improved': caution that output needs checking and improving; P31.
units.anchor: AI is not likely to generate a response that would be seen as quality work

units.why: 'Fact check anything generated with original sources' is a verification rule, P31.
units.anchor: Fact check anything generated with original sources.

units.why: 'You will be responsible for any errors or omissions provided by the tool' makes students own output, P29.
units.anchor: You will be responsible for any errors or omissions provided by the tool.

units.why: 'Cite all A.I. tools used and the generated prompts and outputs' specifies tool, prompt and output in citations, P25.
units.anchor: Cite all A.I. tools used and the generated prompts and outputs.

units.why: 'Failure to do so is in violation of academic honesty policies' makes nondisclosure the violation, P28.
units.anchor: Failure to do so is in violation of academic honesty policies.

units.why: 'Check with your instructor to confirm it is appropriate for the case or circumstance' is an ask-first rule, P10.
units.anchor: Check with your instructor to confirm it is appropriate for the case or circumstance.

units.why: Option 3 says 'the use of artificial intelligence (A.I.)-powered programs is allowed' for the course: permit by default, P02.
units.anchor: the use of artificial intelligence (A.I.)-powered programs is allowed

units.why: 'it is your responsibility as a scholar to make sure you are clearly communicating the A.I. involvement in your work' is a disclosure duty, P24.
units.anchor: clearly communicating the A.I. involvement in your work

units.why: 'all A.I.-generated materials must be fact-checked and confirmed through additional sources': verification rule, P31.
units.anchor: all A.I.-generated materials must be fact-checked and confirmed through additional sources

units.why: The sample phrase 'This paper was generated with the help of GPT-4' shows the in-text acknowledgement wording; a disclosure rule, P24.
units.anchor: This paper was generated with the help of GPT-4
units.frag_start: Please make sure to use phrases

units.why: The appendix item 'Tools Used' requires naming the precise AI tools and how they were used, specific tool details, P25.
units.anchor: A description of precisely which AI tools were used
units.frag_end: long stretches of text, lines of argument

units.why: The appendix item 'Reflection of Usage' requires an account of why AI was used and whether it helped, a reflection, P26.
units.anchor: An account of why AI tools were used

units.why: The appendix item 'Entire Transcript' requires the whole exchange with the AI, P26.
units.anchor: The entire exchange between you and the AI

units.why: The assignment-makeover section says instructors should rework assignments 'regardless of the level of A.I. usage', P35; it gives a three-level scale of makeover.
units.anchor: revamp your assignments to encourage deeper learning regardless of the level of A.I. usage

units.why: Cosmetic change: 'rework elements to make it more difficult for A.I. to respond', an assignment redesign, P35.
units.anchor: rework elements to make it more difficult for A.I. to respond

units.why: 'Run assignments through A.I. to see how well they are processed and make tweaks accordingly' advises instructors to test assignments with AI, a redesign step (P35); P59 would fit instructor AI use but the point is assignment design.
units.anchor: Run assignments through A.I. to see how well they are processed

units.why: Minor renovation: separate 'the process ... from the product', allow AI for research and ideation and have students document process, with the rubric including working with AI; redesign of assignment and grading, P35.
units.anchor: separating the process (brainstorming and planning) from the product (the final submission)

units.why: Minor renovation: 'The grading rubric will include an element of working with A.I.', grading redesigned around AI, P35.
units.anchor: The grading rubric will include an element of working with A.I.

units.why: Major overhaul: 'Rewrite the assignment, integrating the use of A.I. as a major component', so AI use is built into the work; P35 (redesign) with require stance.
units.anchor: Rewrite the assignment, integrating the use of A.I. as a major component

units.why: Major overhaul: students 'will need to document not just how they used A.I. ... but also what aspects of A.I. answers they used', a process-reflection duty, P26.
units.anchor: Students will need to document not just how they used A.I.

units.why: Major overhaul: 'The grading rubric will include an element of the effective use of A.I.', grading redesigned around AI, P35.
units.anchor: The grading rubric will include an element of the effective use of A.I.

units.why: Strategy: 'Integrate discussions on the ethical implications of using A.I. in assignments' prompts students to consider fairness, transparency and privacy; ethics, P53.
units.anchor: Integrate discussions on the ethical implications of using A.I. in assignments.
units.frag_end: privacy aspects of A.I. applications they utilize.

units.why: Strategy: 'Use Google Doc for all writing assignments (File > Version History)' uses version history as process evidence; P40.
units.anchor: Use Google Doc for all writing assignments (File > Version History).

units.why: Strategy: 'Allow students to utilize AI for drafting designated sections of an assignment (e.g., Intros or conclusions)' lets AI produce limited parts of submissions; P16.
units.anchor: Allow students to utilize AI for drafting designated sections of an assignment

units.why: Strategy: 'Ask students to use AI to complete the assignment, and then ... critique the AI work', redesign around AI, P35.
units.anchor: Ask students to use AI to complete the assignment, and then ask them to critique
units.frag_end: what was correct and what was problematic

units.why: Strategy: 'Ask students to provide sources to support and verify AI-generated sources', verification, P31.
units.anchor: Ask students to provide sources to support and verify AI-generated sources.

units.why: Strategy: 'Ask students to submit their own work to AI for feedback, and integrate feedback into work before submission' builds AI feedback into the assignment, P35.
units.anchor: Ask students to submit their own work to AI for feedback

units.why: Strategy: 'Interview students about their work' when plagiarism is suspected, a check of understanding through interviews, P34 (not P57, as it is an assessment tactic rather than a pre-escalation conversation).
units.anchor: Interview students about their work.

units.why: Strategy: 'Take advantage of the AI-writing detector in Canvas Assignments' (SimCheck AI score) recommends a detector to find AI use; P40.
units.anchor: Take advantage of the AI-writing detector in Canvas Assignments.
units.frag_end: quizzes to assignments to take advantage of the AI detector.

units.why: In-class presentations or debates are suggested so students can show understanding and defend their positions, which checks understanding in person; P34.
units.anchor: In-class presentations or debates
units.frag_end: defend their positions effectively in-class presentations or debates.

documents.title: Academic Integrity (graduate catalog policy)
documents.summary: The graduate catalog's academic integrity policy contains a single AI sentence among its plagiarism guidelines. It bars AI-generated materials for credited work without permission.
documents.stance_why: One sentence, 'Students may not use artificial intelligence (AI) generated materials for work submitted for credit without permission', bans AI unless the instructor permits it, so the stance is restrict.

units.why: The graduate catalog lists AI use among academic integrity violations: 'Students may not use artificial intelligence (AI) generated materials for work submitted for credit without permission.' It is a ban-unless-permitted rule (P06, restrict). P36 is not chosen because the sentence states the rule rather than the misconduct handling.
units.anchor: may not use artificial intelligence (AI) generated materials for work submitted for credit without permission
units.policy: Students may not use AI-generated materials for work submitted for credit without permission.

notes: No computing-unit or school policy found. Syllabus resource (Jan 2024) predates the fall 2025 AI policy and may be partly superseded. Catalog document is the graduate version only. In the AI policy, the Permitted Uses list is split into a permission-condition unit (P06) and a uses unit (P12) because they are distinct rules.
